rationale: XGBoost was trained with class-balancing (scale_pos_weight = 4.615), which introduces a +1.53 log-odds shift that pushes scores for applicants with any credit risk upwards (an unweighted 50% risk maps to p ~ 0.82). The test distribution is bimodal: grades A/B cluster strictly below 0.01 (0.0% default rate), while grades C-G cluster between 0.60 and 0.90. The 0.20 threshold safely encapsulates low-risk/prime applicants. The 0.80 threshold captures moderate/transition applicants (n = 402, default rate 47.0%). The 0.83 threshold divides the upper cluster into high (n = 906, default rate 50.7%) and very high risk (n = 892, default rate 53.3%). Observed historical default rates increase monotonically across all four bands: 0.0% -> 47.0% -> 50.7% -> 53.3%.
